header:
Date: 2027-06-03 | Start: 17:00 UTC | Duration: 78 minutes | Venue: All-hands - company-wide Zoom
Attendees: Leadership panel + company All Hands (approx 150 remote)
Deck: internal/ops/q3-priorities-deck (internal link)
Recording: s3://redwood-recordings/2027/06/03/aurora-briefing.mp4
transcript:
[00:00] Ariella Chen: Good afternoon everyone, welcome to the Aurora briefing. Sorry we're a touch late, we had a small infra page but it's resolved. I'll kick off with the agenda — quick health check, three priority bets for the quarter, org/hiring, and then open Q&A.
[00:18] Marcus Liu: Hi all, quick note from infra — the small regression we saw last week in token latency is contained, root cause was a kernel selector mismatch on some GPU families, patch is staged. We'll still run a broader perf sweep per Leah's ask.
[00:32] Samira Patel: Thanks Marcus. On the product side we trimmed our roadmap down to the top bets: 1) Redwood Optimize — actionable batching & cache recommendations, 2) Dedicated stability & capacity autoscaler, and 3) Private onboarding flow (VPC + KMS wiring). Those are what we expect to move to canary in Q3.
[00:52] Diego Ramos: To add, engineering will put an explicit hold on new model catalog additions except critical security patches. The rationale is we need to keep latency SLOs stable while we finish the autoscaler and improve kernel fallback.
[01:07] Leah Novak: On research — we'll prioritize black-box performance diagnostics and a KV cache visibility dashboard. There are times when customers say 'KV cache' and we don't have enough telemetry to prove what happened.
[01:21] Audience: [muted applause emojis in chat]
[01:28] Ariella Chen: Quick people update — Rowan will talk hiring. But first, risk surface: Dedicated is close to oversubscribing at peak hours in our us-west pools unless we add burst capacity. This affects SLA-backed customers and is a top blocker for sales motion.
[01:49] Rowan Ellis: Hiring plan — we request authorization for six IC hires: two infra, two runtime, one product manager, one solutions engineer. We'll also accelerate recruiter partnerships in APAC. Heads will be open next week.
[02:06] Samira Patel: We'll also tighten ship on feature gating — anything that can impact latency will require a Performance Review board sign-off. That'll be triaged by Marcus + Leah + Samira.
[02:18] Marcus Liu: Quick technical aside — fallback policies will be automated: if a high-capacity model is offline, route to quantized variant with a graceful degradation banner for customers. We need marketing/back-end signals to handle the billing nuance.
[02:35] Maya Singh: We'll prepare messaging templates and the usage/cost notes. Also, we need better language for the 'graceful degradation' so customers don't see incorrect expectations.
[02:44] Diego Ramos: On Dedicated autoscale: proposed approach — a two-tier autoscaler. Tier 1: soft autoscale for burst (no SLA change), Tier 2: hard-provisioning for commit customers. We're prototyping thresholds.
[03:00] Ariella Chen: Let's surface a couple of numbers — target: reduce median token latency by 12% for 2-8k seqs by end of quarter, reduce per-token cost by 8% via Optimize improvements, and get Dedicated oversubscription under 5% at peak.
[03:21] Audience: [chat: will the Optimize changes change prompts?]
[03:28] Samira Patel: No, Optimize is mostly infra suggestions and config changes. There'll be a small SDK helper to enable smarter batching but we'll keep prompts untouched.
[03:36] [00:03:50] Nora Kim: Customer success note — we have three high-priority customers in onboarding (RegulaHealth, FinEdge, and BrightForms). They all asked about private deployment timelines and SOC2 in the next 6–8 weeks. We should hurry up on SOC narratives.
[03:56] Ariella Chen: Actionable: Nora, share the SOC2 summary and the gap plan with Sales by Friday.
[04:02] Nora Kim: Copy.
[04:07] [00:04:20] Leah Novak: On the perf sweep — we'll run two passes: synthetic microbenchmarks and a sampled in-prod trace audit. The goal is to validate kernel selector changes and ensure no regression introduced by recent quantization experiments.
[04:24] Marcus Liu: There's also a long tail with legacy CUDA driver versions in some Dedicated hosts — that complicates kernel selections. We'll publish a driver-compat matrix.
[04:35] Diego Ramos: Ops note — we plan a maintenance window for a subset of Dedicated nodes next week; we'll do it in low-traffic windows but teams should expect transient throttling.
[04:48] Samira Patel: Product clarifications: the Private onboarding flow will include an automated KMS handshake and an audit-log forwarder. We want customers to be able to stand up Private in under 2 weeks for standard templates.
[05:02] Ariella Chen: Ok, open Q&A. Please upvote questions in Slido, we'll triage.
[05:10] Employee (Slack): Question for Marcus — how confident are we about the kernel patch rollout? Any rollback plan?
[05:18] Marcus Liu: We're about 70% confident — patch has been tested on canary infra stacks, rollback is the standard blue/green with a fast revert path. We also keep KV cache warmers so cold cuts are minimized.
[05:35] Employee: Will the Dedicated capacity oversubscription require immediate budget?
[05:40] Diego Ramos: Probably short-term burst purchases, but long-term it's a sales-ops pricing and capacity plan. We need to know which customers are high-touch committed and move them to hard-provision tiers.
[05:55] [00:06:00] Samira Patel: On Optimize — we plan to ship the first set of recommendations as a beta for power users. The UI will show estimated cost savings and a risk indicator.
[06:08] Leah Novak: We'll validate the recommendations against historical workloads to reduce false positives.
[06:15] Employee: Any change to the public API?
[06:18] Marcus Liu: Minor SDK helper functions, keeping the main text generation endpoint backward compatible. No breaking changes.
[06:25] [00:06:38] Ariella Chen: Another people note, promotions and leveling will be announced next week; we will also publish our updated career ladder and compensation calibration.
[06:51] Rowan Ellis: On the compensation calibration — we are aligning ahead of offers and expect a +3–5% band uplift for affected bands based on market data. More details in People channel.
[07:04] Employee (quiet): Can we get an incident postmortem template?
[07:08] Marcus Liu: Yes — we'll standardize it. Samira, Leah and I will own the template and circulate it.
[07:15] [00:07:30] Maya Singh: Marketing/comms alignment — we need to be careful with any public messaging that alludes to latency regressions; use 'performance tuning maintenance' language instead. We'll share a PR checklist with legal.
[07:29] Ariella Chen: Legal is looped in.
[07:33] [00:08:00] Q&A continued (rapid-fire):
[08:00] Employee: Are we freezing new features entirely?
[08:03] Samira Patel: Not entirely — only feature additions that can materially affect latency or infra stability are gated. UX and docs are fine.
[08:12] Employee: What's the plan for APAC region support?
[08:15] Diego Ramos: We'll expand Dedicated pools in APAC but on a committed basis. Recruiter work is underway to grow SRE support.
[08:24] Employee: Anything on evals / hallucination monitoring?
[08:27] Leah Novak: Yes — we will integrate a quality monitor in Optimize to surface regression alerts tied to prompt sets and the eval harness.
[08:36] [00:09:00] Ariella Chen: Closing — recap of three measurable goals and owners (Samira: Optimize, Diego: Dedicated, Leah: Perf diagnostics). We'll have weekly 30-minute checkpoints on Wednesdays. Next all-hands will be an end-of-quarter show-and-tell.
[09:00] Nora Kim: For customers in the pipeline — we'll prioritize enterprise sales handoffs; CS will prepare playbooks.
[09:10] Ariella Chen: Thank you everyone, meeting adjourned.
[09:15] [post-meeting quick notes — chat threads with follow-up links]
[09:20] Oliver Park (chat): link to repo with autoscale experiment: github.com/redwood-inference/autoscale-experiments
[09:22] Samira Patel (chat): link to Q3 trimmed roadmap: internal/docs/q3-trimmed-roadmap-v2.pdf
[09:25] Nora Kim (chat): security pack link: internal/security/soc2-gap-plan.xlsx
[09:30] End of recording
notes: Meeting was company-wide; ~150 attendees across timezones
Technical deep-dive items were deferred to a follow-up 60-min technical sync next Tuesday
Hiring and compensation changes were high-salience for many teams
